open_points.subject: publish / withdraw an artifact pointer by Cabinet Kernel
open_points.text: publish an artifact pointer | producer service; the owner for any owner service
open_points.question: When Cabinet Kernel publishes or withdraws a pointer with agent authority, is it confined to the session's granted set (R0-41, R0-46, R0-47)? If it is, what is the refusal? Does Kernel also hold an unconfined producer authority?
options: Kernel publishes and withdraws only with agent authority, confined to the session's set, refused as 'not granted' otherwise
Kernel holds two authorities: an unconfined producer one and a confined agent one
open_points.default_guess: Kernel publishes and withdraws only with agent authority, confined to the session's set; the publish and withdraw rows add 'a project the session is not granted refused'.

open_points.subject: read the latest artifact of a type
open_points.text: read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service
open_points.question: Does 'a service' include Kernel acting for the agent on any project, against R0-41 and R0-46? Or is Kernel confined to granted projects here, as it is for 'list artifacts'?
options: Kernel for the agent only on a granted project; other services as trusted services
any service with a token, unconfined
open_points.default_guess: Same 'who' as 'list artifacts': owner; a trusted service; Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted.

open_points.subject: 'trusted service' versus 'a service'
open_points.text: owner; a trusted service; Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted
open_points.question: Which services count as 'trusted services'? Does Kernel without agent authority count as one? Why do some rows say 'a trusted service' and others 'a service'?
options: trusted service = any service whose own token allows the operation (PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet), never Kernel
the two terms are synonyms
open_points.default_guess: Trusted service means PresuPro, Client Portal and Cabinet, each per its token. Kernel acts only with agent authority. Use one term throughout.

open_points.subject: validate a project reference, for the agent
open_points.text: Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted (R0-46) (R0-41) | exists, active, and why not (`not_found`, `archived`) | — (the answer carries the failure)
open_points.question: What does validate answer when Kernel asks about a project outside the session's set? R0-47 forbids revealing whether that project exists.
options: answers the same as not_found
refuses as 'not granted' for every id outside the set, whether or not it exists
open_points.default_guess: A uniform 'not granted' refusal for any id outside the set, indistinguishable between existing and non-existing projects.

open_points.subject: agent-authority refusals and existence leak
open_points.text: list rooms | ... Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted (R0-46) | ... | unknown project refused as not found
open_points.question: For an agent-authority call on a project outside the set, does the 'not found' versus 'not granted' check order reveal existence (R0-47)? Which refusal does the agent get on list rooms and list artifacts?
options: the set check comes first; every out-of-set id gives the same 'not granted'
not found first
open_points.default_guess: The set check comes first, with one uniform refusal for every out-of-set id.

open_points.subject: restricted customer and project corrections
open_points.text: no new project or correction of a project may name it
open_points.question: Does a restriction refuse any correction of a project that already names the restricted customer, or only a correction that newly names it? R0-51 says 'no project may newly name it'.
options: only newly naming is refused
any correction of such a project is refused
open_points.default_guess: Only newly naming is refused, as in R0-51; reword the table row to match.

open_points.subject: restricted customer in context and reads
open_points.text: while restricted, its data stays stored, reaches no one but the owner
open_points.question: Does `context`, or 'read a project' by a trusted service, still carry the `customer_ref` of a restricted customer? Is it marked as restricted there?
options: customer_ref still answered, no contact data
customer_ref withheld while restricted
open_points.default_guess: customer_ref is still answered, since it is not contact data; State 1 decides the representation.

open_points.subject: caller-supplied project id
open_points.text: What counts as equal content in a project-create replay, and a replay of an archived project's id
open_points.question: The create row and R0-44 say Registry mints every id and a caller supplies none. Do caller-supplied ids still exist anywhere, for example on test instances? If not, should this State 2 item be dropped?
options: no caller id anywhere; drop the item, and replay safety is only R0-36
test instances still accept caller ids per R0-07
open_points.default_guess: No caller-supplied id on create in any instance; ids enter only by import. Drop or reword the State 2 item.

open_points.subject: import projects with their identity
open_points.text: the projects of the running instances under the identities they carry
open_points.question: How does the import receive the running instances' data: an uploaded export file, a direct read of their stores, or something else? Which instances are sources, given that test instance data is never carried over? Can a refused import be retried, given 'once'?
options: owner uploads an export of each named running instance; a refused import may be retried until one succeeds
Registry reads the old stores directly
open_points.default_guess: The owner uploads an export in a format State 1 declares. 'Once' means one successful import; refused attempts may be retried.

open_points.subject: read the agent projection
open_points.text: its id, display name, status, rooms and artifact pointers — no address, customer or other personal value
open_points.question: The display name, room names and pointer uri or payload_ref may contain an address or a customer's name. How is that kept out of the agent projection, and what disclosure class do these fields carry?
options: the display name is declared non-personal and the owner interface warns against personal values
the fields are classed business_confidential and nothing is checked
open_points.default_guess: Class them business_confidential and require the display name to carry no personal value; State 1 records it.

open_points.subject: agent session identity
open_points.text: read the session's access | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session
open_points.question: The session is named by Kernel, so what makes Registry's check 'independent of Kernel' (R0-46, R0-47)? Can Kernel's token act for any registered session?
options: Kernel's token may act for any session it registered; independence covers only the set membership check
each session is bound to a credential Kernel cannot forge
open_points.default_guess: Kernel's token acts for sessions it registered. Registry independently checks set membership against its own store; Kernel remains trusted for the session's name.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror
open_points.text: Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, the Cabinet Web mirror. Each authenticates with its own service token
open_points.question: Does the Cabinet Web mirror get a token, and with what operations and class? R0-27 makes its read conditional.
options: it gets a read-only token without personal_data
it gets no token and loses access
open_points.default_guess: It stays listed as a consumer conditional on a token. Without one it is refused like any unauthenticated caller.
